questions.q: Can AI sound like my brand?
questions.a: Yes, AI can match your brand voice when you train it with your tone guidelines, vocabulary and example replies. It can also adapt to each location by referencing store names, services or menu items where they're relevant. The more replies you review and approve, the closer it gets to how your best team members write.

questions.q: Why do AI replies often sound generic?
questions.a: Off-the-shelf AI tools usually haven't learned your tone, policies or values, so they fall back on bland, corporate phrasing. They also miss regional language and cultural nuance. Replies like a plain thank-you without acknowledging the issue can leave guests more frustrated than before.

questions.q: How do I train AI to use my brand voice?
questions.a: Share your brand tone guide, sample responses and escalation policies, and note any regional differences in tone or service style. Then review and approve early replies so the system learns what a great response looks like. Once it's reliable, let it handle routine replies while your team takes the higher-touch issues.

questions.q: Should AI replies differ between restaurant locations?
questions.a: Small differences can help, as long as every reply still sounds like your brand. A store in a busy city center might suit a more polished tone, while a neighborhood location might feel warmer and more informal. Mentioning the location by name also makes a reply feel personal.

questions.q: How does Momos keep AI replies on-brand across locations?
questions.a: Momos trains its AI on your tone guidelines, brand vocabulary and examples, then adapts replies to each location's context. Your team can review, edit or approve AI-generated replies to build confidence. It works across Google reviews and delivery platforms, so every response sounds consistent wherever it's posted.
